sources.title: Irish Elk
sources.locator: Hall of Advanced Mammals exhibit description
sources.supports: Megaloceros giganteus identity, large deer form and enormous male antlers. Reported maximum spreads and simplified extinction date are not used as exact dimensions or a global last-occurrence claim.
sources.rights: Museum webpage; no open reuse license established. Consulted only.

sources.title: The Irish elk: when and why did this giant deer go extinct and what did it look like?
sources.locator: Why were giant deer antlers so big?; What else can fossils and cave art tell us about the giant deer?
sources.verification: Museum page opened and read; source image download not used
sources.supports: Approximate upper scale of 2 m at shoulder and 3.5 m antler spread; robust cervical/skull support and elongated shoulder vertebrae. Soft-tissue hump and coat markings remain interpreted, not specimen-exact.
sources.rights: Museum text and separately credited artwork; no redistribution license established. Consulted only.

sources.title: Guide to the National Museum of Ireland: Natural History
sources.locator: 2005 edition, printed pages 14–15, PDF page 9; foreground mounted Megaloceros giganteus from Lough Naglack, Co. Monaghan
sources.verification: Original museum PDF retained and page 9 rendered and visually inspected
sources.supports: Whole mounted skeletal proportions, long slender distal limbs, cervical rise, wide bilateral antler beams and irregular palmated distal margins. Display pose and restoration are not asserted to be original life posture.
sources.rights: © National Museum of Ireland, Dublin, 2005; all rights reserved. Text: Nigel T. Monaghan. Photography: Valerie Dowling and Noreen O’Callaghan. Reference-only, excluded from public deliverable.

sources.title: Natural History: Giant Irish Deer skull and antler from Wilton
sources.institution: Cork Public Museum / Cork City Council
sources.locator: Wilton Roundabout find, 1993; skull and detached antler photographs and dimensions
sources.verification: Official page and two original images retained and visually inspected
sources.supports: Skull pedicle placement and antler palm thickness/irregular taper. Reported skull maximum length 0.54 m and detached antler length 1.47 m are contextual specimen measurements, not target-model dimensions. Broken edges are not living anatomy.
sources.rights: Page credits Harri Teague (UCC student, MA in Museum Studies); no open image license established. Consulted only, excluded from public deliverable.
